narratives.Problem: Each deposited PreToolUse command starts the complete Directive CLI router, making Windows edit hooks spend roughly 0.7–1.0 seconds in cold process startup. Cursor ApplyPatch adds a second process through its adapter probe.
narratives.Change: Ship a dedicated lightweight deft-hook executable and deposit it for every host's tool.before registration. Remove the Cursor adapter and its version probe while retaining the existing fail-closed decision path.
narratives.Scope: In scope: hook executable, all agent-host deposits and their health checks, multiplicity coverage, user-facing hook documentation, and release notes. Out of scope: disabling Tier-1 hooks, hostHooks opt-out as a performance solution, resident helpers, and Shell/MCP matcher work.
narratives.Impact: Touches the CLI package bin surface, Cursor projection, shared agent-hook deposit and inspection logic, installer hygiene, focused tests, commands documentation, and CHANGELOG.
narratives.Risks: A malformed fast-path deposit could bypass hook enforcement or leave consumers with stale Cursor adapters. The implementation must preserve host codecs, fail-closed denies, and existing ritual/scope/runtimeAuthority decision logic.
narratives.Approach: Invoke the existing hook-dispatch runner directly from a dedicated bin, route every tool.before command to it, and migrate Cursor ApplyPatch back to the shared direct-write matcher because hook-dispatch already parses its free-form stdin. Recognize legacy registrations as managed so update rewrites them.
narratives.Alternatives: A resident helper would reduce startup further but increases lifecycle and fallback complexity. Keeping an ApplyPatch adapter would still require an additional Node process, so it cannot meet the one-process requirement.
narratives.Dependencies: The existing hook-dispatch parser, core hooks decision surface, and init/update deposit refresh are already available.
narratives.Confirmation: Scott explicitly approved named change hook-dispatch-fast-path on 2026-07-23.
